data.narrative:
Vertical Aerospace is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $50M to date. The comparable universe within Drones & Autonomous consists of eight private peers, including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Waymo, Wayve, and Zipline. There are no public trading comps in this narrow sector.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains seven same-sector peers overall, but filtering by stage, adjacent-stage proximity, and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any single cohort—below the minimum threshold for statistical reliability. An all-sector median approach would introduce excessive noise and is therefore not defensible.

Given the absence of sufficient narrow-set comparables and the inapplicability of public market multiples, this analysis cannot triangulate a valuation range with confidence. Any conclusion would rest on either (1) accepting sparse peer data with acknowledged limitations, or (2) employing alternative methods not yet applied—such as DCF analysis contingent on revenue and capital-efficiency assumptions, or transaction multiples from recent financings within the peer set, if disclosed. The primary uncertainty is the scarcity of comparable transaction or trading data at Vertical Aerospace's scale and stage within its specific subsector.
